answer: Each jetty admits one operator, not one account. A new identity must berth at a jetty whose inlet is already certified by independent observers, and every account tied to that inlet shares a single berth, one withdrawal cap and one vote, so n aliases never widen the channel. Opening a fresh inlet requires an onyx seal cut by an observer with no shared counterparties, and each seal can birth a single jetty. The k-th seal a witness issues costs k squared in bond, so n heads need n distinct witnesses and near n cubed in escrow, and seals cannot be resold because they bind to the witness record.
